roles.title: Capital Management Intern – Summer 2027
roles.description: Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures. Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard. We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position. POSITION SUMMARY: At National Life Group, we are modernizing our business and adapting our customer experience to a digital-first operating model. We aim to activate, engage, inspire, and connect with buying and selling customers to increase production, deepen relationships, and create meaningful connections grounded in our mission and purpose. Measuring progress and performance through meaningful insights is central to our transformation. The Capital Management internship will provide exposure to how a leading U.S. life and annuity insurer evaluates current and projected capital needs, understanding the drivers of changes in capital and risk-based capital ratios, and provide insight into potential capital impacts from business activities, investment decisions, reinsurance deals, and regulatory developments. The intern will collaborate cross-functionally across Finance, Accounting, Actuarial, Risk Management, Investments, and other corporate teams. The Capital Management Intern will support the company’s efforts to monitor, analyze, forecast, and manage its financial strength, capital position, and risks by assisting with updating and validating capital models, analyzing and forecasting changes in regulatory and rating-agency capital, and understanding and communicating capital implications for the company, in addition to activities such as process improvements and documentation activities. This position currently offers an onsite work schedule, with the expectation that you will be in the office four (4) days per week during onsite core days. Our current onsite core days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. The work schedule type and core days are subject to change with advance notification and manager discretion. RESPONSIBILITIES: Update capital analysis on a quarterly and as-needed basis, including data population, error resolution, interpreting results, and preparing presentation materials Assist in the preparation of quarterly Risk-Based Capital (“RBC”) calculation and attribution analysis, including validating and summarizing results Perform impact analysis of proposed regulatory capital changes for RBC and S&P model Collaborate with internal partners to perform assigned duties Improve efficiency of working files and processes Document capital management processes and procedures Perform ad hoc analysis and provide support for capital management activities, responsibilities and communications All other duties as assigned MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Pursuing degree in Finance, Actuarial Studies, Math, or a similar quantitative field Experience with gathering, organizing, cleaning, and interpreting information (e.g. data sets) Working exposure with relational databases (e.g. Microsoft SQL, Access) and writing queries Working exposure using Analytical and Visualization tools, specifically Tableau & Alteryx Ability to translate business needs into effective analytical solutions and models Understanding of foundational financial principles, e.g. interest rates, investments, and financial statements (e.g. balance sheet) Strong analytical skills with the ability to work in a fast-paced finance environment Ability to meet deadlines for recurring reporting and analysis Ability to quickly develop professional relationships with others and effectively communicate using various platforms or methods Proficiency in Microsoft Office, e.g. Excel AI Proficiency Expectations At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength. All associates are expected to: Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work. Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working. Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content. Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products by adhering to National Life's AI guiding principles. Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property. Core Competencies Service Focus - Demonstrates a client centric focus for satisfying one’s external and/or internal customers; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect. Decision Making - Makes sense of complex information, critically evaluates, and creates solutions. Results Oriented - Sets performance and personal goals; Driven to meet or exceed goals and objectives. Plans and Aligns - Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals; Aligns people and skills to tasks and assignments; Evaluates results of work. Demonstrates Learning Agility - Enhances skills and knowledge through continuous learning; Focuses on personal results by establishing stretch goals; Seeks feedback and changes accordingly. Establishes Relationships - Builds partnerships with others to instill trust, collaborate, and meet shared objectives. Communicates Effectively - Actively listens, conveys messages to meet different audience needs, and remains open to new ideas and opinions. Fosters Diversity - Values diversity and difference in thought, experience, and perspective; Promotes an environment that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion; Supports equal and fair treatment for all. HOW YOU SHOW UP : Highly reliable, engaged and possess a customer service attitude Demonstrate effective communication to various areas of the organization (technical and non-technical) Bring creativity, thought leadership, and curiosity to the table; actively participate in forums to contribute and learn Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, i.e. a problem solver’s mindset Eager to learn, ask relevant questions, seek new knowledge, and make connections Enjoy taking on challenges and working towards solutions both collaboratively and independently PROGRAM HIGHLIGHTS: 10-week paid internship (June 1 - August 6) with formal orientation and onboarding Networking opportunities with peers and leaders throughout the summer Cross-Departmental group project focused on an enterprise-wide solution presented at company-wide event Presentation skills coaching sessions Learning opportunities throughout program Access to mentors (former program participants) Base Pay Range . The base pay range for this position is the range National Life reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors, including: prior experience and job-related knowledge; education, training and certificates; current business needs; and market factors. The final salary or hourly wages offered may be outside of this range based on other reasons and individual circumstances. Additional Compensation and Benefits . The total compensation package for this position may also include a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in National Life’s discretionary annual incentive programs, subject to the rules governing such programs. If hired, the employee will be in an "at-will position" and National Life reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. National Life is accepting applications for this role on an ongoing basis and the role remains open until filled. Hourly Pay Range $19 — $28 USD National Life Group® is a trade name of National Life Insurance Company, Montpelier, VT – founded in 1848, Life Insurance Company of the Southwest, Addison, TX – chartered in 1955, and their affiliates. Each company of National Life Group is solely responsible for its own financial condition and contractual obligations. Life Insurance Company of the Southwest is not an authorized insurer in New York and does not conduct insurance business in New York. roles.title: Community Engagement Intern (Summer 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Community Engagement Team Zipline's Community Engagement Team plays an important public facing role in Zipline's operations. They are responsible for building and maintaining strong relationships with local government officials, civic organizations, business groups, neighborhoods, and schools. Their work helps individuals and organizations understand the impact of Zipline's service on the community, job creation, and the future of a logistics system that serves all humans equally. The Role Does creating and maintaining important relationships with multiple layers of stakeholders within local communities come naturally to you? Are you an engaging communicator who drives powerful narratives to create excitement and adoption of big and bold ideas? This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about community building, communications, and social impact. You’ll help design and implement strategies to engage our community members, strengthen partnerships, and support outreach initiatives. What You'll Do Assist in planning, promoting, and executing community events, workshops, and virtual meetups. Support the development of content for newsletters, social media, and other communication channels. Respond to community inquiries and engage with members across platforms. Conduct research on community needs, trends, and engagement strategies. Help track engagement metrics and compile reports on community feedback and outcomes. Provide general administrative support to the community engagement team. What You'll Bring Strong written and verbal communication skills. Passion for community building and social impact. Experience with social media platforms and/or digital tools for community engagement (e.g., Slack, Facebook Groups). Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage multiple tasks. Creative thinker who brings enthusiasm and initiative. Must be able to travel frequently throughout Dallas, Texas, Austin, Texas, Los Angeles, California, OR Phoenix, Arizona. Requires transportation (not company provided) and the ability to independently travel to operational sites, events, communities, and partner locations as needed. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our Dallas, Texas, Austin, Texas, Los Angeles, California OR Phoenix, Arizona office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/Jun to Aug/Sep. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $30 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. roles.description: At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Content Systems is the heart of Lyft's language ecosystem. The team is made up of two distinct disciplines, Content Design and Learning Experience Design, who create and own language across Lyft's in-app experiences that help customers succeed on the Lyft platform. We're looking for a Content Design intern to join our team for the summer. This role will both help design and build our internal content system (think information architecture), and embed in a rotation of design teams as a content design/learning design partner in building products across the Lyft community. Of course, you won’t be alone. You'll work with designers, researchers, marketers, and product managers day in and day out to develop experiences that reach and resonate with riders. This internship will take place in our Toronto office during Summer 2027 . What we're looking for Responsibilities: Support our content system by establishing and translating information architecture to help manage content across Lyft Help teams reconsider existing systems and processes (eg publishing workflows) to align to the new information architecture Support product strategy and vision through content, working on projects as a content designer and learning experience designer Translate complicated concepts into clear in-product copy (UI, notifications, errors, and more) and learning materials Collaborate with designers, visual content creators, researchers, engineers, marketers, data science, product managers, and other stakeholders across tech and ops The ability to translate concepts across the UI, learning center, and knowledge base into connected content objects Manage multiple projects and competing priorities Maintain, evolve and champion the Lyft brand voice and style Skills: Excellent writing skills; ability to demonstrate this in the UX writing, information architecture, or education design space preferred A systems mind that considers the holistic information experience Ability to understand and discuss strategy, metrics, and results A collaborative, proactive mindset Nice to haves: Experience with design tools (Figma) Experience with content management systems (Ditto, Contentful, etc) Knowledge of accessibility best practices Qualifications: Currently pursuing a Bachelors , Masters or PhD degree in a writing or UX-adjacent field like English, Journalism, User Experience, Design, Education, Sociology, Psychology or Creative Writing from a university in Canada , with a graduation date between December 2027 and Summer 2028 (required) Available during Summer 2027 for an internship in Toronto Required: A portfolio must be submitted with your application and should include at least 3 samples/case studies demonstrating one more of the following: UX writing, information architecture, education design. *Note: Great candidates might not have a traditional background or strong experience in this field. That's expected, and we encourage those with the skills above to apply even if you're thinking "I'm not sure this is me" What you'll get from Content Systems Working with us: Guided mentorship from tenured content designers and learning experience designers Hands-on experience designing products with a full-stack tech team Discovering how to do more with more — we're focused on how AI can support us, not replace us Learn to solve product problems from the lens of content design and learning design Good humored, well-intentioned practitioners with over a century of combined content experience (yes, really) Benefits: Mental health benefits In addition to holidays, interns receive 2 days paid time off and 3 days sick time off Subsidized commuter benefits and Lyft ride credits Lyft is committed to creating an inclusive workforce that fosters belonging. Lyft believes that every person has a right to equal employment opportunities without discrimination because of race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, family status, disability, pardoned record of offences, or any other basis protected by applicable law or by Company policy. Lyft also strives for a healthy and safe workplace and strictly prohibits harassment of any kind. Accommodation for persons with disabilities will be provided upon request in accordance with applicable law during the application and hiring process. Please contact your recruiter if you wish to make such a request. Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule — Team Members will be expected to work in the office at least 3 days per week, including on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Lyft considers working in the office at least 3 days per week to be an essential function of this hybrid role. Your recruiter can share more information about the various in-office perks Lyft offers. roles.title: Survey Internship (Summer 2027)
roles.description: At Woolpert, you’ll do work that matters. As a leading global architecture, engineering, and geospatial firm, we help clients solve complex challenges that shape communities, strengthen critical infrastructure, advance technology, and improve the world around us. Here, you’ll collaborate across disciplines, tackle meaningful projects, and build a career defined by growth, opportunity, and impact. Position Overview Seeking a new career challenge? Then Woolpert is seeking you! Woolpert is hiring a Survey Intern to join our Survey and Geospatial team for the 2027 internship program . This full-time internship provides students with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience supporting field and office surveying operations while working alongside experienced survey professionals on a variety of infrastructure, transportation, aviation, utility, and geospatial projects. As a Survey Intern, you will assist with collecting, processing, and analyzing survey data that supports engineering design, construction, mapping, asset management, and community development initiatives. You may contribute to boundary and topographic surveys, control surveys, mobile and terrestrial laser scanning, UAV support operations, GIS data collection, transportation asset inventories, and other geospatial projects that directly impact the communities where we live and work. This intern will be a full-time position for both field and office operations out of multiple locations with opportunities to travel. Woolpert does not provide relocation assistance for interns. Woolpert is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must already possess authorization to work in the country where this position is located. What You Will Do Work as an integral member of a survey field crew and project team. Assist licensed surveyors, survey technicians, and geospatial professionals with field data collection activities. Operate and learn advanced surveying technologies, including GNSS/GPS receivers, robotic total stations, digital levels, data collectors, terrestrial laser scanners, and UAV-related equipment. Support topographic, boundary, utility, construction, and control surveys. Assist with establishing photo control points and ground control for aerial mapping and remote sensing projects. Collect, organize, and process survey data using industry-standard software and workflows. Support the development of maps, plats, reports, and survey deliverables. Follow established safety procedures and maintain a strong commitment to workplace safety. Collaborate with project teams while developing professional problem-solving, communication, and technical skills. What You Will Bring Don't have all of these qualifications? That's okay. We know you're here to learn and grow. We encourage you to apply if you believe this opportunity is a good fit. Currently enrolled in an accredited college or university pursuing an Associate's or Bachelor's degree in surveying, or related field. Familiarity with surveying principles, field procedures, and coordinate systems. Exposure to GNSS/GPS equipment, total stations, laser scanning, or UAV technologies. Experience with surveying and design software such as Trimble Business Center (TBC), AutoCAD Civil 3D, MicroStation/OpenRoads, ArcGIS, etc. Ability and willingness to work outdoors in varying terrain and weather conditions. Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills. Self-motivated with a willingness to learn new technologies and processes. Strong organizational, time management, and problem-solving skills. Ability to travel as needed during the internship. Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record. #LI-MH1 #LI-Onsite Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Pay Range $23 — $27 USD Find out more about what Woolpert has to offer here: http://woolpert.com/about-us/ Woolpert is an equal-opportunity employer. Woolpert is committed to the full inclusion of all individuals. We recruit, train, compensate, and promote regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. This is a real seat at the table: you'll support active searches, contribute to how Prophet shows up to candidates and on campus, and help build the programs that keep our intern community engaged from offer to day one. If you're curious about talent, energized by people, and want hands-on experience at a fast-moving consulting firm — this is it. You'll engage with real candidates on real roles. A clean pipeline and a great candidate experience are both yours to protect. roles.title: UX Research Intern (Summer 2027)
roles.description: At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Lyft is seeking a Mixed Methods User Experience Research Intern to join our team, which aspires to elevate the user experience for our drivers and riders across 300+ cities nationwide. You will conduct research studies, as well as participate in studies alongside more senior researchers from which you’ll gain strong mentorship. You will partner with Design, Product Management, Analytics, and Engineering in order to derive deep insights about our users’ behaviors and attitudes, and communicate results and actionable recommendations across the company. Interns contribute to user-facing products, working side-by-side with top User Experience Research team members in the industry while having autonomy from the get-go. Lyft fosters a collaborative environment in the office, so there's always a sharp mind eager to hear about your next idea. So what's yours? Responsibilities: Design and conduct studies across key Lyft product areas -- independently and in conjunction with more senior researchers. roles.description: The Role We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical intern to join our Operations division under the Middle Office team at Schonfeld in our New York office. You’ll spend ten weeks within our team where you will work directly with Operations senior management and across peer groups in all areas, while being immersed in the culture and atmosphere of Schonfeld, working alongside talented professionals on high profile projects. The Middle Office team at Schonfeld take on a wide range of responsibilities and challenges. They are responsible for the trade life cycle which includes everything from supporting trading and portfolio managers all the way through trade settlement. Throughout the program you will receive formal training, mentorship, and exposure to multiple groups including Core Operations, Asset Servicing, Technology, Market Data, Accounting, Portfolio Finance, and Prime and Executing Brokers. What You’ll Do Trade Lifecycle Management – Support the post-trade processing of all trading activity to ensure trades hydrate all internal systems and get delivered to external partners. Trade Settlement Management – Work with prime brokers and executing brokers to resolve any trade settlement breaks, ensuring efficient operational procedures and reducing risk for the firm. Data Integrity Improvements – Work with the Middle Office team on creating and improving databases in an organized and centralized location. This is a prime opportunity to learn various facets of the different business departments, acquire knowledge of how various asset types function, how data is retrieved and communicated with sell side counterparties, gain an appreciation for all components of data and its investment value to a hedge fund. In working on these operational projects, you will interact and liaise to help us achieve a scalable infrastructure that is efficient and its data integrity in high regard for completeness and accuracy. What You’ll Bring What you need: Interest in gaining Operations experience at a hedge fund Basic understanding of capital markets, investing, and hedge fund strategies A keen analytical eye with high regard for attention to detail We’d love if you had: Working knowledge of Python, SQL, and/or another programming language Experience working with AI to manage projects Prior experience using reporting or analytics tools with data aggregation Our Internship Kick-start your career in finance with the Schonfeld Summer Internship! Over the course of 10 action-packed weeks, you will have the opportunity to build solutions that tackle real-world challenges and leave a lasting impact on the firm. As an intern, you’ll join a close-knit team that is ready to support your growth and accelerate your career. We will pair you with a dedicated manager and a mentor who’ll guide your development over the course of the internship and beyond. Throughout the program, you will have the chance to connect with senior leaders through a series of learning sessions, attend hands-on skills workshops, network at social events and get a behind-the-scenes look at how various functions power the firm. We’ll empower you to bring your ideas to life and make an impact. Who We Are Schonfeld is a global multi-manager hedge fund that strives to deliver industry-leading risk-adjusted returns for our investors. We leverage both internal and external portfolio manager teams around the world, seeking to capitalize on inefficiencies and opportunities within the markets. We draw from decades of experience and a significant investment in proprietary technology, infrastructure and risk analytics to invest across four main strategies: Quant, Tactical, Fundamental Equity and Discretionary Macro & Fixed Income. Our Culture At Schonfeld, we’ll invest in you. Attracting and retaining top talent is at the heart of what we do, because we believe that exceptional outcomes begin with exceptional people. We foster a culture where talent is empowered to continually learn, innovate and pursue ambitious goals. We are teamwork-oriented, collaborative and encourage ideas—at all levels—to be shared. As an organization committed to investing in our people, we provide learning and educational offerings and opportunities to make an impact. We encourage community through internal networks, external partnerships and service initiatives that promote inclusion and purpose beyond the firm’s walls. __PRESENT __PRESENT

We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space. Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart. You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality. If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager. ______________________________________________________________________________ Job Summary: We are seeking highly motivated emerging talent to participate in a 10-week immersive internship program from June 7, 2027, to August 13, 2027. This program offers university students hands-on experience through project-based work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Throughout the program, Interns will have exposure to mentorship, networking, and professional development opportunities. The Government Relations intern will support Voyager Technologies at our Washington D.C. location. The Government Relations Intern will support the Government Relations team with research, analysis, and communications activities related to public policy, government affairs, and the broader legislative and regulatory environment. This internship provides an opportunity to gain exposure to how organizations engage with government stakeholders and monitor policy developments that may impact business and industry priorities. The intern may contribute to projects involving legislative and regulatory research, stakeholder and policy analysis, government engagement, industry research, and development of materials that support the company’s government relations strategy. Responsibilities Conduct research on legislative, regulatory, and policy developments relevant to the company and its industry. Monitor congressional, executive branch, agency, and other government activities and summarize key developments. Research and organize information related to government stakeholders, policymakers, agencies, industry organizations, and other relevant groups. Assist with tracking and analyzing proposed legislation, regulations, policies, and other government actions. Support the development of policy briefs, issue summaries, presentations, internal readouts, and other government relations materials. Attend or listen to hearings, briefings, policy events, and other relevant meetings and prepare concise summaries and key takeaways. Assist with preparation for meetings, briefings, and other government relations engagements. Support the preparation of meeting materials, talking points, background research, and follow-up materials. Conduct research and analysis to support business and government relations priorities. Organize and maintain relevant government affairs, policy, and stakeholder information. Collaborate with internal teams to gather information and support cross-functional government relations initiatives. Participate in team meetings, training sessions, and other learning opportunities. Contribute ideas for improving research, tracking, and government relations processes. Complete assigned projects and deliverables accurately and within established timelines. Requirements Currently enrolled in an undergraduate program at an accredited university, preferably pursuing a degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Government, International Relations, Business, Economics, Communications, or a related field. Demonstrated interest in government relations, public policy, legislative affairs, government, or related areas. Strong research, analytical, and critical-thinking skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear and concise summaries. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment. Ability to learn new subject areas, research tools, and processes quickly. Ability to travel for in-person orientation and program kickoff, as well as for the final presentation at program completion. Preferred Qualifications Previous internship, coursework, academic project, or other relevant experience related to government, public policy, legislative affairs, political science, or business. Experience conducting policy, legislative, regulatory, or industry research. Familiarity with Congress, federal agencies, state or local government, or government affairs. Experience preparing presentations, research summaries, policy briefs, or other written materials. Interest in defense, national security, aerospace, technology, infrastructure, or other policy areas relevant to the company’s business. Experience tracking legislation, regulatory developments, or government activities. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple research or project assignments. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Australia Team Zipline is building its presence in Australia, and we are looking for an exceptional student or recent graduate to join the team as a part-time Australia Expansion Fellow. The Australia team is responsible for developing the partnerships, market strategy and operations required to bring Zipline’s autonomous logistics system to communities across the country. This means working at the intersection of business, government, technology and community to understand where Zipline can have the greatest impact and what it will take to get there. The Role As an Australia Expansion Fellow, you will work directly with Zipline’s Head of Australia on our community engagement strategy. This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend time with our local leadership out in the community, meeting residents, businesses and community organisations, listening to their perspectives and ensuring questions and concerns are addressed. roles.description: About Formlabs: A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem. That’s what we do. At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. From product, design, and marketing specialists to mechanical engineers, software developers and logistics experts, we're building a company so brilliant and diverse that we can tackle any challenge. Manage behind-the-scenes logistics for campus recruiting events (career fairs, info sessions, etc.). Plan and execute social and networking events for current Formlabs interns. Intern Benefits & Perks: Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community And of course… unlimited 3D prints You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you. Through Connected Impact, you'll see how your work influences critical business decisions and drives value across our operations. If innovation and powering the future sounds exciting to you, we encourage you to apply! Unlike a traditional internship, Impact Works offers the opportunity to rotate among multiple nonprofit partners, gaining hands-on experience with a variety of missions, projects, and community needs. Throughout the summer, you'll support short-term assignments ranging from communications and marketing to event planning, volunteer coordination, grant research, and organizational support. Each assignment offers a new opportunity to develop professional skills, build relationships, and experience firsthand the important role nonprofits play in our communities. Launched in 2026, Impact Works supported 22 nonprofit organizations during its inaugural summer. We're looking for curious, creative, and adaptable students who are eager to build on that success while gaining valuable experience in nonprofit management, corporate philanthropy, and community engagement. The Intern responsibilities include but are not limited to: Work directly with nonprofit partners on short-term projects that support their missions and organizational needs. Assist with planning and coordination of community events, volunteer initiatives, fundraising activities, and outreach programs. Develop communications and marketing materials, including social media content, newsletters, digital graphics, and event promotions. Support nonprofit operations through research, data organization, grant prospecting, and administrative projects. Quickly learn each organization's goals and priorities, adapting to new environments and delivering quality work within short timelines. Passion for community service, volunteerism, and making a positive impact. Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work with diverse groups. Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable taking initiative, asking questions, and working independently. Creative thinker with strong problem-solving skills and a collaborative mindset. Proficiency in Microsoft Office or Google Workspace; experience with Canva, social media, photography, or video editing is a plus. Travel Requirements: Must possess a valid driver's license. Ability to travel approximately 75% or more of the time, including occasional overnight travel. Position may be home-based within 30 miles of an EQT office in Pittsburgh, Southpointe, Waynesburg, PA, or Bridgeport, WV. Selected incumbent will be placed into the position that best suits their abilities and experience level. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at one of our offices (Torrance/Idaho Falls/Washington D.C.) and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package if eligible. ABOUT THE ROLE Antares Nuclear is seeking a highly motivated and resourceful Government Affairs Intern to support the company's government affairs, communications, international business development, and commercial business development efforts from our Washington, D.C. office. This position offers a unique opportunity to work on emerging national security and energy policy issues while helping advance the commercialization and international deployment of next-generation nuclear technology. The intern will support research, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and business development initiatives, working closely with Antares leadership and cross-functional teams. The ideal candidate is an excellent writer and researcher, has a strong interest in national security, energy, public policy, or emerging technologies, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where initiative and attention to detail are essential. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: - Monitor congressional activity, federal legislation, appropriations, defense authorization, and executive branch initiatives relevant to advanced nuclear energy and microreactor deployment. - Research and analyze policy developments across the Pentagon, Department of Energy, Department of State, Department of Commerce, NASA, and other relevant federal agencies. - Assist in preparing briefing materials, talking points, policy memoranda, presentations, and other materials for meetings with government officials and congressional offices. - Track engagement with congressional offices, federal agencies, military services, and other key stakeholders. - Identify opportunities to advance policies, programs, and funding initiatives that support microreactor deployment for national security and commercial applications. - Support the development of strategic communications materials that articulate Antares’ mission, technology, and value proposition to government, commercial, and international audiences. - Draft and edit executive talking points, briefing materials, presentation content, website copy, and other communications products. - Monitor media coverage, industry developments, and public discourse related to advanced nuclear energy, national security, and microreactor deployment. - Help translate complex technical and policy issues into clear, accessible messages tailored to different audiences, including policymakers, prospective customers, strategic partners, and the general public. - Assist in developing communications strategies for key company milestones, government announcements, industry events, and strategic partnerships. - Identify opportunities to raise awareness of Antares’ work through relevant publications, industry forums, conferences, and other external channels. - Research international markets and identify countries, government agencies, utilities, defense organizations, and other prospective customers for Antares microreactors. - Assess country-level opportunities based on energy demand, national security priorities, regulatory frameworks, financing mechanisms, and government support for nuclear energy. - Support engagement with U.S. embassies, the State Department, the Foreign Commercial Service, international partners, and prospective overseas customers. - Research foreign government procurement processes, export requirements, financing options, and other factors affecting international reactor deployment. - Prepare country profiles, market assessments, customer briefings, and presentations to support Antares' international growth strategy. - Identify prospective commercial customers and strategic partners across sectors such as data centers, critical infrastructure, industrial facilities, remote power systems, and other energy-intensive applications. - Research customer power requirements, market dynamics, competing energy technologies, and potential use cases for microreactors. - Assist with developing customer presentations, market analyses, business cases, and strategic partnership proposals. - Maintain and update business development pipelines, stakeholder databases, and opportunity trackers. - Support preparation for customer meetings, industry conferences, and strategic partner engagements. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in public policy, international relations, political science, economics, business, engineering, energy policy, or a related field. - Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills. - Demonstrated interest in national security, energy, emerging technologies, international affairs, or commercial strategy. - Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise briefings and recommendations. - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. - Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word, and Excel. - A proactive, intellectually curious approach and willingness to take ownership of assignments. PREFERRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE: - Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to manage sensitive matters and competing priorities in a fast-moving environment. - Experience with congressional offices, federal agencies, think tanks, political campaigns, consulting, or business development. - Familiarity with U.S. national security policy, federal appropriations, international trade, or the energy sector. - Experience conducting market research, developing presentations, or preparing policy and business memoranda. - Foreign language proficiency or international experience. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: - Ability to travel as needed for government, regulator, supplier, customer, and international partner engagements. - Ability to support time-sensitive milestones or incidents outside standard business hours when necessary. LOCATION - We are located in downtown Washington, DC in a space designed for team collaboration and easy access to Capitol Hill, federal government offices, foreign embassies, and DC-based think tanks. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. This is a six-month, full-time co-op with regular exposure to senior People leaders. Please note we will only be considering applications from candidates currently enrolled in Northeastern University's co-op program and located within our Boston, MA hub. This is an in-person role (5 days a week) to support office operations and in-person employee experience. What you'll be doing: People & HR Coordination Support the People team across HRIS data entry, employee changes, and document management, helping maintain accurate and well-organized records Assist with scheduling interviews, coordinating reference checks, and supporting candidate experience throughout the hiring process Help maintain People team trackers, dashboards, and reporting on hiring, onboarding, and employee lifecycle metrics. Draft and proofread internal communications, FAQs, and People team documentation. Help monitor and respond to People team inquiries, answering common questions and routing requests with guidance Onboarding & Employee Experience Support logistics for new hire onboarding, including pre-boarding communications, equipment coordination, and Day 1 setup for Boston-based hires. Partner with IT and People Ops to make sure every new hire has a smooth, well-organized onboarding experience. Assist with employee experience programs (recognition, milestones, internal events), including planning, logistics and execution Support engagement survey logistics, including communications, response tracking, and follow-up coordination. Boston Office Management Support day-to-day operations of the Boston office, including supplies, snacks, mail, vendor relationships, and basic facilities needs. Assist with planning and executing Boston office events, team gatherings, and on-site experiences for visiting team members and executives. Coordinate with building management, security, and vendors to support office operations Partner with the People team to keep the office a welcoming, organized, and on-brand space that supports our hybrid work model. Programs & Projects Contribute to People team projects across areas such as Learning and Development, AI proficiency, performance, and culture initiatives. Help build process documentation, SOPs, and how-to guides that scale beyond your co-op term. What success looks like: Within your first 30 days, you’ve ramped on Later’s People tools and processes, built relationships with key stakeholders, and begun supporting onboarding, coordination, and leading office operations tasks. By 90 days, you’re confidently supporting core workflows (e.g., onboarding logistics, scheduling, and office coordination), contributing to People team projects, and helping manage day-to-day operations of the Boston office with guidance, while identifying opportunities to improve processes and the employee experience. By the end of your co-op term, you’ve gained hands-on experience across HR operations and employee experience, and contributed documentation or improvements that support the team after you leave. You’ll walk away with practical skills and a clear understanding of how a People team operates. What you bring: Currently enrolled at Northeastern University and eligible for a full-time, six-month co-op term. Coursework or interest in Human Resources, Organizational Behavior, Business, Communications, or a related field (or equivalent experience that signals readiness for HR work). Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with a high bar for professionalism when handling sensitive employee information. Comfortable with digital tools (Google Workspace, Slack, project trackers) and quick to pick up new systems like HRIS and ATS platforms. Available to work on-site at our Boston office five days per week to support office management responsibilities. Prior internship, co-op, or part-time experience in HR, People Operations, office management, or hospitality is a plus. Exposure to HRIS, ATS (Greenhouse), or workplace systems is a bonus, not a requirement. Interest in how AI tools are being used to scale HR and operations work. How we work: We will do whatever it takes to win: We win when our customers and creators win. We bring full commitment to outcomes that matter, not just effort. We have no limit to our aspiration: We think big, push beyond what seems possible, and refuse to let conventional thinking set the ceiling. We are relentless: We keep going through ambiguity, setbacks and competing priorities, and we find a way forward. We deeply understand our business: If we don’t have the knowledge, we figure it out. We take ownership of understanding how Later works and what drives results. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves: We bring rigor and accountability without ego, and we make space for each other to do our best work. Our approach to compensation: We take a market-based & data-driven approach to compensation. We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation bi-annually, including performance and market-related factors. Our salaries are benchmarked against market Total Cash Compensation for the geographic location of our job posting. Compensation for some roles is structured as On Target Earnings (OTE = base + commission/variable) while for others it is structured as Salary only. To comply with local legislation and ensure transparency, we share salary ranges on all job postings. Skills, experience and other factors help determine the final salary we offer which may vary from the original range posted. Additionally, all permanent team members are eligible to participate in various benefits plans as part of their overall compensation package. Salary Range: $21 per hour *Co-op team members, independent contractors, and freelancers are not eligible for company benefits. Where we work: We have offices in Boston, MA; Vancouver, BC; and Vancouver, WA. For select positions, we are open to hiring fully remote candidates. We post our positions in the location(s) where we are open to having the successful candidate be located. Diversity, inclusion, and accessibility: At Later, we are committed to fostering a culture rooted in an inclusion-first mindset at every level of the company, embracing the importance of hiring and building teams for culture add rather than culture fit . We openly build and maintain unbiased hiring, pay, and promotion practices to create a foundation for an equitable workplace, paving the way for systemic change. roles.title: Human Factors (Winter Co-Op)
roles.description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW: A seaglider floats, foils, and flies — and every one of those transitions has to make sense to the pilots flying it and the passengers riding in it. Nobody has designed that interface before. As a Human Factors Co-Op, you’ll help shape it: contributing to concept sketches, UI/UX standards, and the usability evaluations that keep the interface safe, intuitive, and ready for certification. As part of the Systems team, you’ll be joining a group of driven, collaborative, and talented engineers who take pride in solving complex technical challenges and making an impact as a team. We hold a high bar for engineering rigor, move quickly, think boldly, and rely on our teamwork to push boundaries and bring entirely new technology into the world. If you’d rather sketch and test a real interface than read about one, and you want hands-on experience on a vehicle nobody has built before, we’d love to have you on the team! What You'll Do: - Contribute to new feature concepts. Bring ideas for how pilots and passengers interact with the seaglider human interface. - Help build out our design standards. Contribute to REGENT’s UI/UX standards and design language. - Support safety and usability evaluations. Help plan and run evaluations of the seaglider human interface. - Help define human factors requirements. Support requirements definition and draft test procedures. - Partner across engineering disciplines. Work with engineers across systems, software, and flight test to bring HF findings into the design. What We’re Looking For: - Working toward a relevant degree. Pursuing a degree in Human Factors Engineering, Engineering Psychology, or a related field. - Some exposure to aviation or maritime contexts. Coursework, research, or personal flying, boating, or sailing experience. - Comfort with prototyping and communication. Proficiency with rapid prototyping tools (e.g., Figma); excellent written and verbal communication, including technical documentation. - Self-motivated and adaptable. Comfortable with shifting priorities in a startup environment. Who We’re Looking For: - Curious about people, not just tech. You want to know why someone struggles with an interface, not just that they do, and you’re excited to go find out firsthand. - Hands-on, not just theoretical. You’d rather sketch a quick mockup or run a small usability test than write a memo about what one might find. - Comfortable without a precedent. A seaglider cockpit doesn’t look like anything that exists yet. You’re energized by that, not looking for a template to follow. - Present for the work. Evaluations and test days don’t always land on a tidy schedule, and you’re ready to show up when the work needs you. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

roles.title: International Policy Intern
roles.description: WHO WE ARE Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant. Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach. Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions. WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION - You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world. - You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals. - Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey. - Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent. YOUR IMPACT Proxima Fusion is looking for an International Policy Intern to join the Partnerships and Public Affairs Team in Munich. You will work closely with the International Policy Team and contribute to Proxima's engagement with EU institutions, national governments and international organisations. Fusion is one of the fastest-moving industries in the world and European and international policy will shape how quickly it reaches the market. This internship offers direct exposure to that process and the opportunity to take on substantive responsibility from the start and be involved across a broad range of policy files, from EU funding and industrial policy to the regulatory frameworks for fusion. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Monitor EU policy, regulatory and financial developments, and analyse their impact on Proxima's business to anticipate opportunities and risks. - Research and analyse policy issues relevant to fusion energy at EU and international level. - Prepare briefings and background documents for meetings with EU policymakers, regulators, government representatives and other stakeholders. - Support the development of policy proposals, position papers and consultation responses for European institutions. - Support the coordination of government engagement across jurisdictions in Europe and globally, including bilateral meetings, delegation visits and international forums. - Support Proxima's participation in industry associations and policy events. - Work with Proxima's business and technical teams to keep policy and business priorities aligned, and share policy insights across the company. WHO YOU ARE - Enrolled in or a recent graduate of a degree program in European Studies, Political Science, International Relations, Law, Public Policy, Economics, or a related discipline. - Solid understanding of European Union decision-making structures and legislative procedures. - Exceptional analytical, drafting, and synthesis capabilities, with a track record of distilling policy subjects into business-language. - Full professional proficiency in English. Additional languages preferred. INTERVIEW PROCESS - Recruiter Interview (30-60 min) - Technical Screening (30 min) - Technical Panel (3x60 min) *This role sits at "L1" of our framework, please inquire during the recruitment process for further information. At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

Inventory Manager – High Value Devices Function: Operations – Asset & Inventory Control Inventory Type: High-Value Electronic Assets Tools Used: Manual Registers & Google Sheets Work Mode: On-site Role Overview The Inventory Manager will be responsible for end-to-end custody, tracking, and reconciliation of high-value inventory, primarily iPhones and related accessories such as SD cards and card readers. This role demands strict control, zero tolerance for mismatches, and complete documentation discipline. No inventory movement is allowed without entries, and physical stock must always tally with records. (Morning Shift - 7 am to 4 pm; Evening Shift - 4 pm to 2 am) Key Responsibilities 1. High-Value Inventory Ownership Take complete ownership of high-value devices and accessories . Ensure serial-number–level tracking for all devices. Maintain zero loss and zero undocumented movement . 2. Inward Inventory Management (IT → Inventory) Receive devices and accessories from the IT team. Verify: Quantity Serial numbers Physical condition Record all inward movements immediately in: Manual registers Google Sheets Escalate any mismatch, damage, or discrepancy without delay. 3. Outward Inventory Management (Inventory ↔ Field Ops) Hand over inventory from: Inventory to Field Ops (FO) Field Ops back to Inventory Ensure no item goes out without prior entry . Capture details including: Item name and serial number FO name / ID Date and time of handover Expected return date Avoid all verbal or informal handovers. 4. Returns, Reconciliation & Control Receive returned inventory and re-verify serial numbers and condition. Update return entries on the same day. Perform daily reconciliation between: Physical stock Google Sheets Items with Field Ops Track overdue or missing items and follow up proactively. 5. Documentation & Audit Readiness Maintain clean, structured Google Sheets trackers. Ensure inventory area access is controlled. Support audits and internal checks as required. Maintain high compliance standards for asset handling. Skills & Requirements Mandatory Experience handling high-value inventory or assets . Strong working knowledge of Google Sheets (filters, basic formulas). Experience with manual inventory registers . High attention to detail and accuracy. Preferred Background in inventory, warehouse, logistics, or operations. Experience managing electronic devices or serialized assets. Key Traits Strong ownership and accountability Process-driven with a zero-error mindset High integrity and discipline Comfortable working under strict controls Performance Metrics 100% match between physical inventory and records Zero undocumented inventory movement Zero asset loss due to process lapses Timely reconciliation and reporting Our Values Empathy, Trust & Candor We put ourselves in the shoes of our colleagues and customers and don’t shy away from uncomfortable conversations, instead building trust through honest and direct feedback. roles.description: Operations Intern, Talent Development & Training Hillel International Role Overview The Talent Development & Training team is seeking a highly organized, proactive, and collaborative Talent Development Operations Intern to ensure the seamless execution of HillelU’s growing portfolio of professional development programs and experiences. HillelU provides learning and development opportunities to more than 1,200 Hillel professionals across the organization. As our portfolio continues to grow, this role will provide the operational support needed to deliver high-quality professional development experiences consistently and efficiently—from virtual training and cohort programs to immersive in-person leadership development experiences. This role will serve as a key member of the Talent Development & Training team, taking ownership of the systems, logistics, data, and processes that support the participant experience. The ideal candidate is someone who loves turning plans into action, can anticipate details before they become problems, and is energized by making complex programs feel seamless. What You’ll Do Program Operations & Delivery Support the operational execution of assigned HillelU programs and learning experiences, from initial planning through post-program follow-up. Coordinate session setup, registration, materials, technology, and other operational needs. Manage pre- and post-program communications, including reminders, pre-work, and logistics. Provide or coordinate day-of technology and administrative support for virtual and in-person programs. Partner with facilitators and Talent Development colleagues to ensure they have the information and support needed for successful program delivery. Create and maintain repeatable processes, templates, and checklists that make program delivery more efficient and consistent. Identify operational challenges and proactively develop solutions. Program Data, Evaluation & Reporting Collect, organize, maintain and report on participation and program data. Pull and upload data across relevant systems and ensure program records remain accurate and up to date. Coordinate post-program evaluation processes, including evaluation communications and data collection. Develop regular reports and dashboards that help the Talent Development team understand participation, engagement, and program outcomes. Support analysis of program data to identify trends and inform future planning and decision-making. Partner with colleagues to improve how HillelU tracks and communicates program impact. Leadership Development & Event Logistics Support the operational delivery of select high-touch programs and experiences, including Kaplan Supervisory Leadership Program and Accelerate. Coordinate event logistics including hotels, catering, travel, participant communications, materials, schedules, and other event needs. Manage participant travel reimbursements and other program-related expenses. Coordinate across facilitators, participants, vendors, internal partners, and other stakeholders to ensure a seamless experience. Provide on-site operational support for select HillelU professional development experiences, as needed. Systems & Process Improvement Maintain systems for tracking HillelU programs, participants, logistics, and outcomes. Look for opportunities to streamline administrative processes and reduce manual work. Create documentation and standard operating procedures to support consistency and continuity across the HillelU portfolio. Help the team leverage technology and data more effectively in the delivery and evaluation of learning programs. Support implementation of new tools, systems, and processes as HillelU continues to evolve. Team Partnership Serve as a collaborative operational partner to Talent Development colleagues, helping translate program ideas into executable plans. Support multiple concurrent projects and priorities while maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Provide visibility into project status, upcoming deadlines, and operational needs. Take ownership of projects and follow through independently while knowing when to escalate questions or challenges. Contribute to a collaborative, positive, and service-oriented team culture. Who You Are Highly organized and detail-oriented , with the ability to manage many moving pieces without losing sight of the big picture. A strong project manager who can establish timelines, track details, and ensure work moves forward. Proactive and solutions-oriented , with a natural instinct to anticipate needs and troubleshoot challenges. A strong communicator who can build relationships and communicate clearly with a wide range of stakeholders. Comfortable with technology and data , and excited to learn new systems and tools. Service-oriented , with a strong commitment to creating excellent experiences for participants, facilitators, and colleagues. Able to work independently , take ownership, and exercise good judgment. Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple simultaneous priorities. Proficient in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce, Zoom, learning management systems, event platforms, or similar tools is a plus. We encourage both current college students and recent graduates to apply for this role. What You’ll Receive $17/hr up to 20 hours/week In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience in program operations, project coordination, data and evaluation, event logistics, and talent development while working alongside a team that designs and delivers professional development for Hillel professionals across the organization. You’ll have the opportunity to see how learning experiences are designed, delivered, evaluated, and improved and to build skills that translate across nonprofit, education, Human Resources, and business environments. About Hillel International In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.
